claims.allowed_wording: Even when the raw sequence is IID, overlapping windows make the derived feature sequence non-exchangeable.
claims.name: T2 exchangeability counterexample
claims.prohibited_wording: Overlapping windows are always non-exchangeable for every statistic / all BPI covariance structures.

claims.allowed_wording: Under fixed-M, the equal-weight two-DGP overlap-induced naive calibration distortion exceeds 10 percentage points (D=0.5354, basic CI [0.5210,0.5494], Holm p<0.05).
claims.name: P1_D_OV_M0 (fixed-M overlap)
claims.prohibited_wording: Overlapping windows necessarily produce severe Type-I inflation in every DGP / condition.

claims.allowed_wording: Under fixed-T, the equal-weight two-DGP stride/overlap naive calibration distortion exceeds 10 percentage points (D=0.5330, basic CI [0.5194,0.5462], Holm p<0.05). The distortion pattern is stable across both budget regimes.
claims.name: P2_D_ST_M0 (fixed-T stride)
claims.prohibited_wording: The distortion is identical in every DGP, or universal across all conditions.

claims.allowed_wording: The scalar overlap mean example shows a long-run covariance vs permutation marginal covariance mismatch; the scalar conclusion does not extend to the fixed-BPI covariance matrix without proof.
claims.name: T4 process-level covariance mismatch (Omega != Gamma_0)
claims.prohibited_wording: Omega != Gamma_0 for scalar means therefore implies the multi-dimensional scan limit law necessarily differs.

claims.allowed_wording: DMB-R1 exhibits over-1-percentage-point conservatism at the IID non-overlap end (D=0.0266, basic CI [0.0224,0.0308], Holm p<0.05).
claims.name: P3_D_CONS_M1 (DMB conservatism)
claims.prohibited_wording: DMB universally restores nominal calibration across all finite-sample conditions.

claims.allowed_wording: For shape change, BPI exceeds MOMENTS in size-standardized power by +0.938 (95% CI [0.9297,0.9461]).
claims.name: H1 shape-change size-standardized power difference
claims.prohibited_wording: BPI is universally superior to MOMENTS for all alternatives.

claims.allowed_wording: For mean shift, MOMENTS exceeds BPI by -0.946 (95% CI [-0.9534,-0.9384]); the reversal indicates representation selectivity, not universal superiority.
claims.name: H1 mean-shift size-standardized power difference
claims.prohibited_wording: Reported as a BPI superiority paper; or construction adjusted to make BPI look better.
